cur:catacombs-arles-trinity-spouses.summary: Three tiers of richly carved figures – lid and two registers of the chest – surround a shell with the portraits of a married couple. The scenes include the creation of Adam and Eve by three figures (whence the name 'of the Trinity'), Christ's miracles and episodes of Peter. It is among the finest Roman imports at Arles.
facts: It was discovered in 1974 and measures 103 × 205 × 111 cm, according to the museum.
Like the Dogmatic Sarcophagus in the Vatican, it shows the creation scene with three similar figures, often read as the Trinity.

cur:catacombs2-commodilla-turtura-virgin.summary: The Virgin sits frontally on a jewelled throne with the Christ Child on her lap, both framed by golden haloes; the Child holds a scroll. On either side stand the martyrs Felix and Adauctus, buried in this catacomb, and the saint at the left lays his hand on the shoulder of Turtura, the widow in dark clothes holding a scroll, presenting her to the Mother of God and her Son. An epitaph below, set up by her son, commemorates her.
facts: English Wikipedia describes the 'tomb of Turtura' as built for a woman by her son, with a fresco of her, the two martyrs and the Madonna and Christ Child; the Commons record dates it to 528.
It stands near the small underground basilica of Felix and Adauctus, re-excavated under Pope John I (523–526) for the martyrs' cult.
cur:catacombs2-commodilla-turtura-virgin.notes: Which martyr stands on which side is not stated in the sources consulted.
